newsitem.title: USA: U.S., Japan shipping talks to resume next week.
newsitem.headline: U.S., Japan shipping talks to resume next week.

text.p: U.S. and Japanese officials will resume talks next week to try to end a dispute over Japanese port practices, the U.S. Maritime Administration said on Friday.
The two sides, working to an April 14 deadline, met throughout Friday, the third day of talks in Washington this week, the Maritime Administration said.
If no agreement is reached by the deadline, the United States has said it will impose a $100,000 surcharge on each Japanese vessel docking in U.S. ports.

The Federal Maritime Commission voted to impose the surcharge in retaliation for what it called costly and restrictive practices by the Japan Harbor Transportation Association, which it said discriminated against foreign vessels.
Japan has urged the United States to withdraw the sanctions, and port workers in Japan have staged protests in opposition to the U.S. move.
The Maritime Administration said it would make no further statement on the negotiations before the talks resume in Washington next week.
